plug_ins.missing_input: Historical policy term / writing pattern for exact premium on-leveling
plug_ins.justification: Current exposure listings show annual policies, while historical daily writing weights are not supplied.
plug_ins.limitation: If historical writings were materially seasonal or policy terms differed, annual OLFs would change.

plug_ins.missing_input: Trend-from date for annual premium exposure trend

plug_ins.limitation: Does not reflect within-year exposure seasonality.

plug_ins.limitation: If these percentages measure a different rate-change basis than intended for earned-premium on-leveling, OLFs may be biased.

plug_ins.missing_input: Layer-specific emergence pattern for BF and Cape Cod
plug_ins.selected_value: Use supplied ground-up incurred CDFs as layer emergence proxies
plug_ins.justification: No layer-specific CDFs or triangle are supplied, but the requested comparison requires an emergence pattern.
plug_ins.limitation: BF and Cape Cod do not literally develop each claim and then relayer unreported claims; their layer results are comparison estimates, not exact develop-then-layer projections.

warnings: The claim listings are thresholded: Non-Cat > $50,000 and Cat > $250,000.

For 2024 Commercial Cat claims, a claim just below the $250,000 listing threshold could reach about $509,950 after the selected 2024 loss trend and 1.900 ground-up CDF, so omitted claims could make a small contribution to the 500k xs 500k layer. No omitted-claim load was fabricated.
The 2024 loss experience is valued at 2024-09-30 while the 2024 premium denominator uses full-year Projected GNEPI as instructed.
No workbook loss triangle was used; the Chain Ladder-basis projection is deterministic claim-list development using the user-supplied CDFs.
limitations: Layer 1 Commercial 2024 may be understated by thresholded Cat claims that are not listed but could cross the $500,000 attachment after trend and ground-up development.
BF and Cape Cod use ground-up CDFs as layer emergence proxies; layer-specific emergence could differ.

The 65% BF prior is much higher than observed fitted layer loss ratios and materially drives BF results in immature years; it should be viewed as a sensitivity unless it is independently calibrated to these layer/premium bases.
Uniform writing and July 1 exposure midpoint approximations are used for premium adjustment.
Occurrence limits, annual aggregate deductible, and reinstatements are intentionally excluded per user instruction.
